title: Sobetirome in WWOX research
summary: Retain as a glial maturation probe. Defer pediatric WWOX trial priority pending local exposure and functional first-sheath evidence.

graph.evidence: Neonatal lineage maturation and adult remyelination increase.
graph.inference: Free drug at a developing axon remains unmeasured.
graph.hypothesis: Glial thyroid-receptor engagement could bypass a neuronal constraint.
graph.experiment: Measure first stable sheaths and conduction with exposure and hormone matched.

evidence: In neonatal mice, the mature share of labeled callosal cells increased from about 39% to 54%. In adult Myrf repair, the fraction of myelinated axons rose from 45.5% to 60.9%.
After oral parent in a separate mouse model, total brain drug was about 0.265 ng/g. Residual blood can influence this value. A separate parenteral experiment detected parent in perfused brain.
inference: Glial marker induction, sheath initiation and conduction are separate outcomes. Systemic thyroid feedback can change the baseline during chronic exposure.
hypothesis: If engaged glia can bypass the WWOX neuronal constraint, first stable sheaths and function should recover on WWOX axons.
experiment: At measured free parent and matched T3/T4, compare reciprocal neuron and glial genotypes. Read receptor response, stable new sheaths per eligible axon and patterned conduction.
limits: The registered X-ALD studies enrolled no participants. Pediatric endocrine tolerability, WWOX exposure and functional rescue remain open.
